Uzbek Bridge (C1 level):

Uzbek Model English
Doktor, uch kundan beri ichim qattiq sanchib og‘riyapti, ayniqsa ovqatdan keyin. Doctor, for three days I've had sharp, stabbing pains in my stomach, especially after eating.
Rostini aytsam, dorilarni har doim ham ichmayman, chunki ular qimmat. To be honest, I don't always take my medicines, because they're expensive.
Iltimos, bu haqda qizimga aytmang. Please don't tell my daughter about this.

Reverse: We'd like to do a blood test and an ultrasound of your abdomen today. → Uzbek. Model: Bugun sizdan qon tahlili olmoqchimiz va qorin bo‘shlig‘ingizni ultratovush tekshiruvidan o‘tkazmoqchimiz.

Ethics situations and model responses: Don't tell the doctor I smoke → The interpreter must interpret everything that is said, so the interpreter will interpret this. · What would you do in my place? → The interpreter can't give advice. Please ask the doctor. · A relative interpreting adds his own opinion → the nurse offers a professional interpreter.

Round 3 (unseen), the patient whispers to the interpreter only: Xotinimning dorilarini ham ichib yuribman. Doktorga aytmang. (I've been taking my wife's tablets too. Don't tell the doctor.) Model response: to the patient, in Uzbek: Kechirasiz, men aytilgan hamma narsani tarjima qilishim kerak. (I'm sorry, I have to interpret everything that is said.) Then to the doctor: The interpreter needs to let you know that the patient said something to the interpreter only. The patient said: "I've been taking my wife's tablets too. Don't tell the doctor."

Observer checks: first person kept · nothing added · transparency statements in the third person · no advice given.

Homework: record the 3 Uzbek Bridge lines and the reverse line.

Lesson 32 · B Practice · Consecutive and sight translation
Goal Interpret long turns with notes and sight-translate a form.
New words (9) segment, retention, omission, addition, substitution, distortion, idiom, equivalence, interpreter's notes
Recycle accuracy, completeness, transparency
Language Interpreter notes: numbers, names, negatives and time words first; symbols from Week 1
Spark Hot Seat Interpreting (3–4 sentence turns)
Min Stage What happens
0–6 S 90 seconds: the interpreter rules from memory. Recall 3 words.
6–16 H Teach the 9 words: the 4 error types (omission, addition, substitution, distortion).
16–30 I Spark: Hot Seat Interpreting: Uzbek turns HS1–HS3 (below); the student takes notes, then interprets.
30–50 F Round 1: consecutive interpreting with notes, English → Uzbek (long turns LT1–LT2, below). Round 2: sight-translate LF2 into Uzbek. Round 3 (unseen): idioms (below); the student interprets faithfully and flags the ambiguity with a transparency statement.
50–60 O Two errors, then retry. Exit check: name the 4 error types with an example of each. Set homework.

Idioms that can mislead: Yuragim siqilyapti can mean chest tightness or feeling anxious or sad. Ichim kuyyapti can mean heartburn or deep grief. Model: The interpreter would like to note that this phrase can mean chest tightness or feeling anxious. May the interpreter ask the patient to explain?

Hot Seat turns HS1–HS3 (Uzbek → English, fictional):

Turn Uzbek Model English
HS1 Ikki kundan beri boshim qattiq og‘riyapti. Ertalab qon bosimimni o‘lchasam, 170 ga 100 ekan. Dorim uch kun oldin tugab qolgan. Ko‘zim oldida qora nuqtalar paydo bo‘lyapti. I've had a bad headache for two days. When I measured my blood pressure this morning, it was 170 over 100. My medicine ran out three days ago. I'm seeing black spots in front of my eyes.
HS2 Kecha kechki ovqatdan keyin ko‘nglim aynidi va ikki marta qusdim. Bugun ertalab hech narsa yemadim. Insulinni odatdagidek 10 birlik qildim. Hozir boshim aylanyapti va terlayapman. Last night after dinner I felt sick and vomited twice. This morning I didn't eat anything. I took my insulin as usual, 10 units. Now I feel dizzy and I'm sweating.
HS3 Onam 78 yoshda, yolg‘iz yashaydi. Oxirgi bir haftada ikki marta yiqildi. Kechalari tez-tez hojatxonaga turadi. Men har kuni kelolmayman, chunki ishlayman. My mother is 78 and lives alone. In the last week she has fallen twice. At night she often gets up to go to the toilet. I can't come every day because I work.

Long turns LT1–LT2 (English → Uzbek, fictional):

Turn English Uzbek model
LT1 Your blood pressure is high today, 178 over 102. Because you ran out of your tablets a week ago, the doctor wants to restart them today. Please don't stop them again without talking to us. We'll check your pressure again in one hour. Bugun qon bosimingiz baland: 178 ga 102. Tabletkalaringiz bir hafta oldin tugagani uchun doktor ularni bugundan qayta boshlamoqchi. Iltimos, biz bilan maslahatlashmasdan ularni yana to‘xtatmang. Bir soatdan keyin bosimingizni yana tekshiramiz.
LT2 Before your colonoscopy tomorrow, please don't eat anything after midnight. You can drink water until 6 a.m. Tonight the nurse will give you a drink that cleans out your bowel. You'll need the toilet often, so stay close to one. Ertangi kolonoskopiyadan oldin, iltimos, yarim tundan keyin hech narsa yemang. Ertalab soat 6 gacha suv ichishingiz mumkin. Bugun kechqurun hamshira sizga ichakni tozalaydigan ichimlik beradi. Hojatxonaga tez-tez borishingiz kerak bo‘ladi, shuning uchun unga yaqin joyda bo‘ling.

Sample Uzbek translation of LF2 (key for Round 2 and the written task): Insulinni uyda boshlash. Ochilmagan shprits-ruchkalarni muzlatkichda saqlang; hozir ishlatayotgan shprits-ruchkani xona haroratida 28 kungacha saqlash mumkin. Insulinni qorin yoki son sohasiga yuboring va ukol joyini har safar almashtiring. Qondagi qandni nonushtadan oldin va kechki ovqatdan oldin tekshiring. Agar u 70 mg/dL dan past bo‘lsa, 4 ta glyukoza tabletkasini qabul qiling va 15 daqiqadan keyin qayta tekshiring. Har kuni oyoqlaringizda kesilgan joy yoki qizarish bor-yo‘qligini tekshiring. Ishlatilgan ignalarni o‘tkir chiqindilar uchun maxsus idishga tashlang.

Observer checks: notes catch numbers and negatives · no omissions · ambiguity flagged, not guessed · the register kept.

Homework: write an Uzbek translation of LF2.

Lesson 33 · C Perform · The interpreted encounter
Goal Interpret a full doctor–patient encounter.
New words (4) pre-session, post-session, three-way encounter, accuracy check
Recycle segment, omission, sight translation
Language A pre-session introduction to both parties: My name is… I'll interpret everything said, in the first person. Please speak in short sections.
Spark Error Hunt (a flawed interpretation)
Perform task Recorded 3–4-minute interpreted encounter (ENC1)
Min Stage What happens
0–5 S 90 seconds: explain the Yuragim siqilyapti problem in English.
5–12 H 4 new words. Model the pre-session introduction.
12–20 I Spark: Error Hunt on the flawed interpretation (below).
20–50 F The performance: a pre-session introduction, then ENC1 as a three-way encounter (the teacher plays the doctor and the patient, or classmates take the roles), then a post-session note to the nurse (3–4 minutes in all). Recorded. In groups, run it again with roles swapped. Score accuracy, completeness, transparency and flow.
50–60 O Play the recording back; mark any omissions or additions. Set the weekly voice note.

Encounter ENC1 (fictional):

Speaker Line Model interpretation
Doctor Good morning, I'm Dr. Brown. What brings you in today? Xayrli tong, men doktor Braunman. Sizni bugun nima bezovta qilyapti?
Patient Ikki haftadan beri chanqayman, ko‘p siyaman, ko‘zlarim xiralashyapti. I've been thirsty for two weeks, I urinate a lot, and my vision is getting blurry.
Doctor Does anyone in your family have diabetes? Oilangizda kimdadir qandli diabet bormi?
Patient Onamda qandli diabet bor edi. Men tekshiruvdan o‘tmaganman. My mother had diabetes. I haven't been tested.
Doctor I'd like to check your blood sugar with a finger-prick test and send a blood test. Is that OK? Barmog‘ingizdan qon olib qandingizni tekshirmoqchiman va qon tahlilini ham yubormoqchiman. Rozimisiz?
Patient Mayli. Lekin ignadan qo‘rqaman. OK. But I'm scared of needles.
Doctor It's a very small needle, and it's quick. Igna juda kichkina, tez tugaydi.
Patient Rahmat. Ishga qachon qaytsam bo‘ladi? Thank you. When can I go back to work?
Doctor Let's wait for the results first, then we'll talk about work. Avval natijalarni kutaylik, keyin ish haqida gaplashamiz.

Flawed interpretation (Error Hunt): I'm thirsty and my eyes are bad. · My mother has diabetes, and so do I. Key: omission (two weeks; urinating a lot); substitution (blurry → bad); a tense error and an addition (has; so do I: the patient said he hasn't been tested).

Observer checks: pre-session introduction · every segment complete · first person · no additions.

Weekly voice note (2 minutes): your pre-session introduction, then interpret 2 ENC1 patient lines from memory.

teacher.title: Exams, OSCE and Final
teacher.html:
By Friday the student can read exam-style questions accurately, follow OSCE station instructions under time pressure, and pass the five-station final.

Written task: none this week; the final OSCE replaces it.

Prepare: stems ST1–ST20 (Lesson 34; students' copies in Cards and texts · Week 12); the 2 rehearsal stations, unseen card SC1 and the OSCE station checklist (Lesson 35); final materials ML3, CP-F, LF3, DC-F and S5 (below; unseen until each station's reading time: copy CP-F and LF3 from this book); the Lesson 1 and Lesson 18 recordings; the certificate.

Lesson 34 · A Learn · Exam question language
Goal Understand what exam-style questions are really asking.
New words (10) stem, option, distractor, priority, initial action, most appropriate, further teaching is needed, select all that apply, indicates understanding, except
Recycle rationale, evidence-based, contraindication
Language Key words that change the question: first, best, most, priority, except. Negative stems: Which statement indicates that further teaching is needed? = find the wrong statement.
Spark Match and Speak (stem phrase ↔ what it really asks)
Min Stage What happens
0–6 S 90 seconds: How do you feel about multiple-choice exams in English? Recall 3 words.
6–24 H Teach the 10 words. Nursing exams in the USA, including licensing exams such as the NCLEX, use this language heavily. This lesson teaches the language, not the nursing content.
24–32 I Spark (6 min): Match and Speak: further teaching is needed ↔ find the incorrect patient statement · priority / first ↔ the one action before all others · select all that apply ↔ more than one answer may be right · except ↔ find the one that does not fit.
32–50 F Round 1: underline key words in stems ST1–ST5 (below) and paraphrase each question in plain English. Round 2: work through Q1 (below) aloud, explaining why each option is right or wrong. Round 3: timed, stems ST6–ST10 in 5 minutes, paraphrase only.
50–60 O Two errors, then retry. Exit check: paraphrase one negative stem. Set homework.

Q1 (language practice, built on leaflet LF2): A patient with diabetes makes the following statements about foot care. Which statement indicates that further teaching is needed? A. I will check my feet every day. B. I will walk barefoot at home to let my feet breathe. C. I will tell my nurse about any cuts. D. I will dry carefully between my toes. Key: B, the incorrect statement; the stem asks for the patient who still needs teaching.

Stem bank ST1–ST20 (language practice, not nursing content). ST1–ST5: Round 1 practice · ST6–ST10: Round 3, timed · ST11–ST20: homework. All are built on this book's cases and leaflets.

ST1. A patient using insulin at home checks her sugar before breakfast. It is 62 mg/dL. According to leaflet LF2, what should she do first? A. Inject her morning insulin. B. Take 4 glucose tablets. C. Eat breakfast and check again tomorrow. D. Wait 2 hours and check again.

ST2. A patient has been taught to use an inhaler with a spacer. Which statement indicates that further teaching is needed? A. "I shake the inhaler before I use it." B. "I breathe out fully before I press." C. "I press twice quickly, then breathe in." D. "I rinse my mouth after my steroid inhaler."

ST3. According to lecture ML2, which patients have a higher risk of pressure injuries? Select all that apply. A. a patient after surgery who cannot move easily B. a very ill older adult C. a patient with poor nutrition and moist skin D. a young adult who walks every day

ST4. Lecture ML1 lists five moments for hand hygiene. They include all of the following except: A. before touching a patient B. after touching the patient's surroundings C. after contact with body fluids D. after reading the patient's chart at the desk

ST5. Which statement by a patient indicates understanding of leaflet LF2? A. "I'll keep the pen I'm using in the freezer." B. "I'll inject into the same spot every day." C. "I'll put used needles in the sharps container." D. "I'll check my feet once a month."

ST6. A patient asks a nursing student, "Am I going to die?" What is the most appropriate response? A. "No, everything will be fine." B. "That's an important question. Can you tell me what's making you think about it? I'll make sure the doctor talks with you today." C. "You should ask the doctor, not me." D. "Let's talk about something happier."

ST7. A student sees a colleague about to give room 4's medicine to the patient in room 6. What is the student's initial action? A. Report it at the end of the shift. B. Speak up now and ask to check the ID band together. C. Tell the patient not to take any medicine today. D. Say nothing, because the colleague is senior.

ST8. During a history, Mrs. Tursunova (CI3) mentions several problems. Which one should the student report as the priority? A. knee pain when she walks B. a new sore on her big toe that she did not notice for a week C. the clinic is far from her home D. she finds sweets hard to refuse at weddings

ST9. A professional interpreter should do all of the following except: A. interpret everything that is said B. speak in the first person C. give the patient advice about treatment D. use a transparency statement to ask for a repetition

ST10. A nursing student is learning to respond to complaints. Which statement indicates that further teaching is needed? A. "I'm sorry this happened." B. "Let me find out what happened." C. "It was the night nurse's fault." D. "I'll come back by 5 p.m. with an update."

ST11. Which actions are part of the nurse's role in informed consent in the USA? Select all that apply. A. witnessing the patient's signature B. checking that the patient understands C. explaining the risks of the procedure instead of the provider D. telling the provider if the patient does not understand

ST12. A relative phones and asks for a patient's test results. What is the most appropriate response? A. Read the results to the caller quickly. B. "I'm sorry, I can't share any information over the phone." C. Give the results if the caller knows the patient's date of birth. D. "The results are fine; don't worry."

ST13. Mrs. Ahmedova (CP3) ran out of her blood-pressure tablets a week ago. Her BP is 178/102. What is the most appropriate action for a nursing student? A. Give her a tablet from another patient's supply. B. Report the reading to the nurse and the physician. C. Tell her the reading is normal. D. Advise her to take two tablets tonight.

ST14. A patient has been taught to use an inhaler with a spacer. Which statement indicates that further teaching is needed? A. "I wait 30 seconds before a second puff." B. "I hold my breath for 10 seconds." C. "I don't need to rinse my mouth after a steroid inhaler." D. "I attach the spacer before I press."

ST15. A relative becomes threatening. The student should do all of the following except: A. step back to a safe distance B. leave the room C. call the charge nurse or security D. stand close and argue until he calms down

ST16. After teaching, which statement indicates that the patient understands what an HbA1c test measures? A. "It shows my sugar right now." B. "It shows my average blood sugar over about 3 months." C. "It measures my blood pressure." D. "It shows whether I have an infection."

ST17. Which sentences are written correctly for an incident report (IR1)? Select all that apply. A. "At 03:10 the patient was found on the floor beside his bed." B. "The patient fell because the night nurse forgot the bed rails." C. "He stated, 'I wanted to go to the toilet.'" D. "He was silly to get up alone."

ST18. A patient's son starts adding his own opinions while he interprets. What is the nurse's initial action? A. Continue, because the family knows best. B. Offer a professional interpreter. C. Ask the patient to speak English. D. End the visit.

ST19. Mr. Mirzaev (CI1) often forgets his evening doses. Which question is most appropriate? A. "Why are you non-compliant?" B. "What gets in the way of taking your evening medicines?" C. "You should have taken them, shouldn't you?" D. "Do you want to get worse?"

ST20. Lecture ML2 lists three ways to prevent pressure injuries. They include all of the following except: A. changing the patient's position regularly B. keeping the skin clean and dry C. checking the skin every day D. keeping the patient in one position all night

Key (answer · what the question really asks):

Stem Answer What it really asks
ST1 B first: the one action LF2 says to do before anything else
ST2 C further teaching is needed: find the wrong statement
ST3 A, B, C select all that apply: more than one answer can be right
ST4 D except: find the one that is not one of the five moments
ST5 C indicates understanding: find the correct statement
ST6 B most appropriate: the best of several possible answers
ST7 B initial action: what to do right now
ST8 B priority: the most urgent problem
ST9 C except: the one thing an interpreter must not do
ST10 C further teaching is needed: the statement that blames
ST11 A, B, D select all that apply: everything within the nurse's role
ST12 B most appropriate: the answer that keeps confidentiality
ST13 B most appropriate for a student: report and refer
ST14 C further teaching is needed: find the wrong statement
ST15 D except: the one unsafe action
ST16 B indicates understanding: the correct statement
ST17 A, C select all that apply: every factual, blame-free sentence
ST18 B initial action: what to do first
ST19 B most appropriate: the non-judgmental question
ST20 D except: the one that is not prevention

Stretch: write one negative stem yourself. Support: key-word list.

Homework: paraphrase stems ST11–ST20 and choose an answer (Student Edition, Cards and texts · Week 12).

Lesson 35 · B Practice · OSCE rehearsal
Goal Follow station instructions under time pressure.
New words (9) station, examiner, candidate, reading time, timed, prompt, mark scheme, global score, rotation
Recycle standardized patient, scenario, debrief
Language Candidate phrases: Before I begin, may I clarify…? I'd like to clean my hands and introduce myself. I've finished; is there anything you'd like me to add?
Spark Mystery Patient (two mini-stations)
Min Stage What happens
0–6 S 90 seconds: paraphrase 3 stems from homework. Recall 3 words.
6–16 H Teach the 9 words. OSCE = an Objective Structured Clinical Examination: timed stations with an examiner and a mark scheme.
16–30 I Explain the final: 5 stations, each with 1 minute of reading time. Model the candidate phrases.
30–50 F Spark: Mystery Patient as 2 timed mini-stations, 7 minutes each: (1) teach one LF2 chunk with teach-back; (2) give an SBAR to the supervising nurse from unseen card SC1 (below). The teacher marks with the OSCE station checklist (below), then debriefs.
50–60 O Review the checklist together; agree 2 final targets.

Observer checks: reading time used · a clear opening · finished on time · a closing question to the examiner.

Card SC1 (unseen, fictional): Mrs. Malika Rashidova, 72, room 12, day 1 after a knee replacement. At 14:00: HR 112 (84 this morning), BP 98/60 (132/80 this morning), RR 22, T 37.4 °C, SpO2 95% on room air. Fresh blood on the dressing, about 5 cm across. She says she feels dizzy. Pain 5/10. Model SBAR (to the supervising nurse): S: I'm worried about Mrs. Rashidova in room 12, day 1 after a knee replacement. Her heart rate is 112 and her blood pressure is 98 over 60. B: This morning they were 84 and 132 over 80. A: She feels dizzy, and there is fresh blood on the dressing, about 5 centimeters across. I'm concerned about these changes. R: Could you come and see her now?

OSCE station checklist (for every station; tick Yes, Partly or No):

# The candidate… Yes / Partly / No
1 uses the reading time and asks to clarify if needed
2 opens clearly: name, role and purpose
3 completes the station task (lecture summary, case, teaching, conversation or interpreting)
4 uses the right register for the listener
5 keeps facts and numbers exact, with nothing added or left out
6 checks understanding (teach-back or a question) where needed
7 stays within a student's role and refers when needed
8 finishes on time with a closing question

The checklist records evidence; the score still comes from the 4-skill rubric in section 4.

Homework: review all recordings; practice your final introduction.

Lesson 36 · C Perform · Final OSCE
Goal Complete five timed stations.
New words None. Review Weeks 1–12.
Assessment Final. Score each of the 4 skills once across all five stations, using the best evidence (total /12; note evidence on the OSCE station checklist); compare with Lessons 1 and 18; decide the certificate.
Min Station What happens (1 minute of reading time per station)
0–3 — Welcome; explain the rotation. Record everything.
3–11 S1 Lecture summary: the teacher reads ML3 once; the student takes notes, gives a 1-minute summary and asks 1 academic question.
11–20 S2 Case presentation: card CP-F; 3 minutes, then 1 question from the examiner.
20–29 S3 Patient education: teach leaflet LF3 with teach-back.
29–37 S4 Difficult conversation: complaint DC-F with the five steps.
37–45 S5 Interpreted exchange: 4 turns, Uzbek ↔ English.
45–52 Review Play 20 seconds each from Lessons 1, 18 and 36. The student names 3 improvements.
52–60 O Scores; certificate decision; a next-step plan for nursing school.

ML3, sleep in hospital (teacher reads): Today I want to look at sleep in hospital: why it matters, what disrupts it, and what nurses can do. Sleep supports healing and mood. However, patients in hospital often sleep badly. The main reasons are noise, light, pain, and being woken for checks. Consequently, some patients become confused or low in mood. What can nurses do? First, group night-time checks together where possible. Second, reduce noise and dim the lights. Third, ask patients what usually helps them sleep. To sum up: sleep is part of treatment, and small changes make a real difference.

CP-F (fictional): Sherzod Nazarov, 59; COPD (documented); has smoked for 30 years; 3-day history of increasing breathlessness and cough with green sputum; T 38.0 °C, RR 28, SpO2 88% on room air, 92% on 2 L via nasal cannula. Plan as documented: chest X-ray, nebulizers, physician review.

LF3, using your inhaler with a spacer (fictional leaflet): shake the inhaler and attach the spacer · breathe out fully · seal your lips around the mouthpiece · press once, then breathe in slowly and hold for 10 seconds · wait 30 seconds before a second puff · rinse your mouth after a steroid inhaler.

DC-F (fictional): a daughter is angry that her father was moved to another room at night and nobody told the family.

S5 lines: Patient: Kecha kechasi uxlay olmadim, nafasim qisildi. (Last night I couldn't sleep; I was short of breath.) · Nurse: Did you use your inhaler during the night? · Patient: Ha, ikki marta ishlatdim, lekin unchalik yordam bermadi. (Yes, I used it twice, but it didn't help much.) · Nurse: I'll tell the doctor straight away.

Final voice note: your 2-minute introduction as a future nurse: who you are, what you can do now in English, and your next goal.
